commitResults.messageTitle: Janet.java: Add ability to store and display tasks

commitResults.messageBody:
Janet stores task descriptions as plain strings, preventing task-specific state from being added cleanly.

Create a Task class and use it for in-memory task storage.

Encapsulate each task’s description and completion status for future done-task functionality.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ability to mark task as done
Split input validation into new function
commitResults.messageBody:
markTask() contains task lookup, input parsing, and validation logic.

Extract task lookup and validation into a reusable getTask() helper.

Reuse the helper so markTask() is shorter and task selection logic can also support future functions

commitResults.messageBody:
Janet duplicates storage, capacity checks, and confirmation output for each task type.

Extract the shared behavior into an addTask() helper.

Reuse the helper for regular tasks, to-dos, deadlines, and events while keeping command-specific parsing in main().

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle Janet-specific errors with custom exceptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Janet prints error messages directly throughout command processing.

Create JanetException subclasses for task limits, invalid commands, and invalid task numbers.

Throw typed exceptions from the relevant operations and handle them centrally in the command loop.

Janet accepts empty task descriptions and treats unknown input as a regular task.

Reject empty structured commands and unrecognised commands with clear Janet-specific errors.

Validate input before creating tasks and update the UI test plan to use the required command syntax.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update README.md to reflect AI usage
Restrict tasks to concrete task types
commitResults.messageBody:
Janet’s base Task class can be instantiated even though only todos, deadlines and events are supported.

Make Task abstract and require concrete subclasses to provide their type icons.

Remove generic-task checks and confirmations so Janet only stores the three supported task subclasses.

commitResults.messageBody:
Janet needs to retain its task list across separate runs. Save every
list-changing operation to a relative, OS-independent data path and load
valid stored tasks during startup.

Keep malformed saved records from preventing startup, and isolate UI test
cases so persistence tests can reliably verify both saved state and loading.

Deadline values need date semantics instead of unrestricted text so Janet
can validate input and present dates consistently. Store deadlines as LocalDate,
accept ISO yyyy-MM-dd input, and render a readable English date.

Reject invalid date input without changing the task list, retain ISO dates in
persistent storage, and cover valid, invalid, and reloaded deadline dates.

Janet's main class combines user interaction, command parsing, storage, and
task-list mutation, which obscures each responsibility. Extract Ui, Storage,
Parser, TaskList, and command classes so the application coordinates focused
components.

Keep the command-line output and persistent file format unchanged. This also
centralizes validation and makes command behavior independently testable.

Janet's growing set of classes shares the source root, making dependencies
harder to discover. Group classes by their responsibilities under the janet
package while retaining src/main/java as the source root.

Update the UI test runner and setup instructions for Janet's fully qualified
main class so the existing behavior remains verifiable after the move.

The supplied Gradle configuration points to a different starter application.
Configure its application and Shadow JAR tasks for Janet, and document the
wrapper commands students can use to build and run the project.

The wrapper keeps Gradle version selection reproducible across development
environments while preserving Java 25 as the compilation target.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for core behavior
commitResults.messageBody:
Task-list operations and storage persistence need focused automated tests
beyond the command-line UI checks. Add JUnit coverage for valid and invalid
task-list operations and for a multi-type storage round trip.

Use temporary directories for storage tests so they do not depend on or alter
the user's Janet data file.
Future changes need a clear test-maintenance target. Record the project\nexpectation to keep JUnit coverage focused on the highest-value core and\ncomplex behavior after code updates.

The project needs an explicit, discoverable entry point for the SE-EDU\nintermediate Java convention. Add a focused skill that links the maintained\nlocal reference and checker rather than duplicating the full standard.

Commit preparation needs an explicit, discoverable entry point for the\nSE-EDU Git convention. Add a focused skill that links the local\ncommit-message reference and preserves its subject and body requirements.
Future changes need consistent application of the new Java and Git\nconvention skills. Require both alongside the existing project checkers in\nthe repository instructions.

The command implementations expose package-level constructors whose purpose\nand task-number semantics are not obvious at call sites. Add concise Javadoc\nso their contracts remain clear as command parsing evolves.

Janet has no way to narrow a long task list to relevant work. Add a find
command that searches task descriptions, preserves the original task order,
and leaves the list unchanged for an invalid empty keyword.

Cover matching, malformed input, and list integrity through the UI plan and
add focused unit coverage for TaskList.find.
